column1: # How a name in this project's ledgers maps to Debian package names, for the
# B2 exclusions (#619, ADR 0073). The ledgers spell tools the way their
# (`:wshada`)` — and select-b2.sh excludes by exact package name, so without
# this table a tool this project has already met could be selected again under
#   name      the spelling as it appears in the ledger, verbatim
#   packages  ;-separated Debian package names, or `-` when the tool has no
#             Debian package at all (a pip-only tool, a Rust binary the
#             project fetched from GitHub, a repository name)
#   source    which ledger spells it this way (for a reader; not checked)
# count.py b2-selection holds this file two ways: every name in the five
# spike/outcome-funnel.tsv, spike/upstream-reports.tsv) that is not itself a
# package in b2-exclusions.txt must have a row here, and every package a row
# names must be in b2-exclusions.txt. A name that IS a package name needs no
# What it cannot hold: the packages column is written from memory of the
# archive. A package this table does not name for a tool the project met is
# the gap wall W0 exists for — a selected target that turns out to be one of
# those becomes a W0 row, and this table is not corrected after the fact.
